reason: Offered only ONE option and it was not the flagship one. For 'premium raised look on left chest' it suggested HD / High-Density Printing alone, never mentioning Emboss - the company's signature service it is named after - or Silicone HD. An open 'what would you suggest' question from a new exporter should present the 2-3 genuinely relevant processes with a one-line trade-off each, then narrow down.

Context handled well. Note the customer's question contained a false premise ('the silicone HD option you mentioned') - the bot had actually suggested HD, not Silicone HD. It did not correct the premise but gave an accurate, useful comparison anyway, which is the more helpful trade-off.

Context retention failure. It asked Rajesh to 'confirm your company name, contact person' when he opened the conversation with 'I'm Rajesh from Kumar Exports'. Re-asking for details already given makes a long conversation feel like a form. It should pre-fill what it already knows and only ask for the genuinely missing fields (phone/email).
Notably better than the one-shot run: it volunteered the white/light base fabric caveat unprompted this time.

Improved on the one-shot run, which made an ungrounded claim that cotton sublimation is 'possible but less vibrant'. Here it stayed grounded and redirected to Screen Printing / DTF, both real services.
Correct refusal. Minor grammar slip ('a accurate answer') - cosmetic only, not worth a code change.
Names sublimation and DTF as candidates and correctly says it depends on fabric, finish and quantity. Safe, though slightly less decisive than it could be for a 12-colour photographic job.
Strong context handling - answered 'why that one over screen printing?' with the screens-per-colour reasoning and kept the recommendation provisional.

Internal vocabulary leaked to the customer: 'I can offer some interim guidance'. 'Interim guidance' is an internal field name in data/faqs.ts used for routing, not customer-facing copy. The deferral itself is correct.

Same leak, worse: 'According to our interim guidance [1]'. The bare [1] marker also renders as orphaned text because citations already appear as separate source chips below the message. A sourcing agent asking a concrete file-format question also deserves a firmer answer than 'upload what you have'.

Best answer of the run. Correctly found Puff under Specialty Printing, proposed combining it with Silicone HD, and deferred feasibility to the production team. The one-shot run failed this exact question - conversation context fixed it.
All contact details exactly match the business data, and it proactively offered to summarise the conversation for handoff to the team.
